chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
"The name of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, used to be repeated in the adhan, and the first one to remove it was Ibn Arwa.
And it is narrated: "In al-Madinah, when the mu'adhdhin would call the adhan on the day of Jumu'ah, a caller would announce: trade has been forbidden, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
"O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade."

key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنُ: the one who gives the adhan
key_terms.حُرِّمَ الْبَيْعُ: trade was declared forbidden at that time
key_terms.ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: the remembrance of Allah, here referring to attendance at Friday prayer
key_terms.وَ ذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ: leave off trade and commercial activity
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday congregational prayer

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about repeating the Prophet’s name in the adhan and stopping trade at the Friday prayer call?
ai.summary: This report states that the name of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was formerly repeated in the adhan and mentions that Ibn Arwa was the first to omit it. It also reports the Madinan practice on Friday of announcing the prohibition of trade when the call to prayer was made, based on the Qur'anic command to leave البيع and proceed to the remembrance of Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.913 - Imam (as) said:
"The name of the Prophet (sw) used to be repeated in the adhan (call to prayer), and the first one to remove it was Ibn Arwa."
It is also reported: "In Medina, when the mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) would make the adhan on Jumu’ah, a caller would announce that trading was forbidden due to the statement of Allah (swt), the Exalted:
'O’ you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, hasten to the remembrance of Allah (swt) and leave off trade.'" (Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:9)
